source_basis.note: Synthetic asymmetry continuation only; no empirical claim that candidate systems are actually 1.5x-5x slower.

asymmetric_model.latency_family: code-like CV=3.3 correlated lognormal plus independent 1% x10 side straggler stress
asymmetric_model.statistical_reveal: precommitted pair order; completion cannot reorder or select signs
asymmetric_model.dedicated: candidate and incumbent have separately reserved side slots bc and bi with bc+bi fixed
asymmetric_model.pooled: all side tasks share total side capacity; launch priority fixed pair-major before outcomes; paired result remains quarantined until both sides complete and prefix reveal permits use
asymmetric_model.sampling_status: Coarse synthetic screen. Individual cells used 500-700 fail and 150-220 commit stage draws per action and 80000 full-run resamples; comparisons are topology-level rather than exact deployment estimates.

scale1_5.interpretation: At mild asymmetry pooling did not beat equal dedicated in this Monte Carlo cell; tuned unequal allocation improved only about 0.34%.

scale5.refined_high_candidate_allocation_screen: Separate 20..31 candidate-slot sweep found 26/6 q95=13710.025 versus pooled q95=13717.967 on the same refined draw set; pooled was within about 0.06% of the best tested dedicated allocation.
scale5.interpretation: Extreme asymmetry makes equal reservation visibly wasteful, but a tuned dedicated split can still match or slightly beat pooling.

scale2.interpretation: All three are within about 0.3%; fixed reveal head-of-line dominates side-pool imbalance.

interpretation: Shared pooling is mainly an allocation-robustness mechanism, not a cure for the statistical head-of-line barrier. Under symmetric or mild asymmetric side latencies it provides little or no q95 advantage over equal dedicated pools.

As candidate latency becomes 2-3x larger, pooling begins to recover some imbalance versus an equal split, but the gain is only about 0.5-1.3% at total capacity 32 and about 0.8% at total capacity 64 in the tested cells.

If the latency asymmetry is known, a tuned unequal dedicated split generally matches or slightly beats pooling. Pooling's value is therefore avoiding the need to know or continually retune the asymmetry.
At extreme 5x asymmetry, pooling beat equal 16/16 by about 2.6% in the coarse screen and came within about 0.06% of the best refined dedicated 26/6 split on a separate matched draw set.

Doubling total side capacity from 32 to 64 makes allocation differences even smaller, which further supports the diagnosis that heavy-tail fixed-reveal head-of-line, not side-pool imbalance, is the dominant residual latency source.
scope_guards: All asymmetry factors are synthetic stress parameters. They are not measured candidate/incumbent latency ratios.
The 5x coarse and refined screens use different Monte Carlo draw sets; only the within-screen comparisons are meaningful.
Pooled launch order was fixed independently of outcomes. A work-stealing policy that consults completion-derived semantic information would require a new validity proof.
The q95 wall objective still excludes peak-slot reservation price, queue interference, cancellation delay and actual monetary cost.
No evidence here supports racing nondeterministic replicas and selecting the first output; that can change the paired outcome law.

frontier.action: Stop spending effort on side-pool topology unless deployment asymmetry is large or unknown. The measured residual is head-of-line dominated; move to validity-preserving straggler control.

Test prelaunch-only latency predictors to order the already-fixed task set, with predictor provenance frozen before paired outcomes. Measure whether predicted-short-first order reduces head-of-line q95 without changing task composition or conditional sign validity.

Test semantics-preserving deterministic side replication/hedging with fixed replica arbitration independent of semantic content; if replica outputs can differ, do not use race-to-first as an evaluation outcome without a new estimand and validity analysis.
Add explicit peak-slot reservation and queue-interference price before preferring total side capacity 64 over 32.

exact_next_action: Construct a prelaunch latency-predicted ordering stress: generate outcome-independent latency covariates before execution, sort the fixed task set using only those covariates, keep paired statistical reveal in that precommitted predicted order, and compare q95 wall/occupancy/unresolved against random/fixed order under predictor error and sign-latency dependence.
